statements.t: Unless the context otherwise requires, references to “we,” “us,” “our,” and “the Company” are intended to mean the business and operations of Hyperfine, Inc. and its consolidated subsidiaries.

We believe these learnings will enable us to further improve our product and develop new services and tools in the future.
Building upon this foundation and our expertise in ULF brain imaging, we plan to develop new imaging applications, broadening the range of clinical uses for our proprietary technology.
While these technical innovations may increase our research and development expenses, we expect them to have a positive impact on our results of operations and profitability in the future.

As we continue to invest in research and development of our products and sales and marketing, we expect to continue to incur negative cash flows from operations and recurring net losses for the foreseeable future until such time that our product and services sales generate enough gross profit to cover our operating expenses.

However, we can provide no assurance that our product and service sales will generate a net profit in the future or that our cash resources will be sufficient to continue our commercialization and development activities.

The offering of our Class A common stock pursuant to the prospectus supplement dated November 22, 2023 was also terminated such that no further offers or sales will be made pursuant to such prospectus supplement, effective as of December 29, 2025.

The 2026 Shelf is expected to include a prospectus supplement covering up to an aggregate of $50.0 million in shares of Class A common stock, which amount is included within, and not in addition to, the $150.0 million registered under the 2026 Shelf, that we may issue and sell from time to time, through B.

We expect that our existing cash and cash equivalents, together with proceeds from the sales of our products and services, will enable us to conduct our planned operations for at least the next 12 months.

estimates.t: Our management's discussion and analysis of our financial condition and results of operations is based on our condensed consolidated financial statements, which have been prepared in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America.

statements.t: Management continues to expect revenue for the full year 2026 to be approximately $20 to $22 million, representing 55% growth at the midpoint as compared to full year 2025.
Management continues to expect net cash burn 1 for the full year 2026 to be approximately $26 to $28 million, representing a 10% decline at the midpoint as compared to full year 2025.

The Company has not provided a reconciliation of full year 2026 net cash burn guidance to forward-looking net change in cash and cash equivalents, because the amount and timing of future financing proceeds cannot be predicted without unreasonable efforts.
The Company expects to file a new registration statement on Form S-3 to replace its existing shelf registration statement, which is scheduled to expire in November 2026.
Management uses non-GAAP measures to compare the Company’s performance relative to forecasts and strategic plans and to benchmark the Company’s performance externally against competitors.

A reconciliation of the Company’s full-year 2026 net cash burn guidance to the most directly comparable GAAP measure is not provided because the Company is unable to predict certain components of such measure, including future financing proceeds, without unreasonable efforts.
